side_a: CC 3.1.3.2 "A proposal seats at most once. A widening that cites an acceptance an admitted widening has already consumed is not admissible, so one invitation never admits twice."
side_b: CC 3.2 "The founder's standing **`membership:proposal:v1`** is then addressed to any requester — its `subject_key_ids` is resolved at acceptance rather than fixed at proposal"
note: A builder of 'a proposal seats at most once' spends the standing proposal on the first joiner, so an open room admits one person per proposal; a builder of CC 3.2 admits every requester. Admission rule (5) ('P has not already seated K'), CC 3.2 and the CC 8.10 guard (spent per acceptance) support the per-joiner reading; the 'seats at most once' sentence needs the standing offer excepted.

side_b: CC 3.4.12: a single `provider`-rung capacity attestation **plus** the adjudicated binding
note: the confidence rule asks the panel rung for any high-scope domain, naming medical and financial; the T1 row admits a provisional binding with enumerated health and asset-preservation powers on one provider-rung attestation plus the order, and the admission predicate asks only for a live incapacitated row at any level. side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.2 When subject `s` emits `consent:state:revoked` (or an admitted `withdraws`) against target `T`, substrate watches for producer compliance
side_b: CC 3.3.1 Breach is therefore: the window passed **and** the row is still present with none of the three composers against it.
note: The subject's own admitted withdraws is one of the two events that start the deletion clock, and it is also a withdraws against T. Read literally no breach can follow a withdraws-started clock; CC 3.3.1 step 5 ('Producer withdraws, supersedes or hard-deletes') means the producer's act. One reader lets the subject's withdrawal discharge the producer, the other raises the breach. manifests/reactions.json copies the literal reading (clock from 'withdrawn of target', breach unless 'withdrawn of target').

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1: "They are re-emitted as new rows, signed and cosigned again, with the readers in `subject_key_ids`."
side_b: CC 2.1: "At a targeted scope the keys a row lists in `subject_key_ids` are keys within the row's audience and no others."
note: A non-public licence is re-emitted to validating readers who are outside the roster ('never by widening the roster') by naming them in subject_key_ids; CC 2.1 refuses a targeted row naming a key outside its audience (subject_outside_audience), lists the families that deliver outside a cohort (proposal invitee, key grant recipient, owner's node) without licensure, and makes subject_key_ids the party the row is about, with the subject's standing to retract. One implementer refuses the re-emitted licence, the other delivers it and gives the reader a subject's standing over it. CC 2.1 and CC 5.2 are the home of the audience rule; the licensure registration states no outside reach.

side_a: CC 3.1.1: "signed by the founder (or a current `moderate`-holder) of the community it names; one live row per community"
side_b: CC 3.2: "The listing is the founder's own row"
note: Who may sign and amend a room's listing. The emitter cell of the CC 3.1.1 row admits a current moderate-holder beside the founder; CC 3.2, the home of the public room, makes the listing 'a federation-scoped scores row by the founder' and the founder's own. A rename is a supersedes, which CC 2.4.1 gives to the same attester, so under CC 3.1.1 a moderator's rename of the founder's row is either refused or a second live row against 'one live row per community'. The data follows CC 3.1.1 for attest (founder, moderate) and CC 2.4.1 for supersede (author only). A node built from CC 3.2 refuses a moderator-signed listing; one built from CC 3.1.1 admits it.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 the removal action ([CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md) `takedown_notice`); content does not survive
side_b: CC 4.5.3 **That key MUST hold the `takedown` duty over the content's community under [CC 4.5.5](#4.5.5) (a) as-self or (b) delegated from an accountable root**
note: The ladder makes an undefended report (no keep and no vote carried) a hard removal by takedown_notice, but that case arises only when no moderator or steward acted, and no node signs a notice (CC 4.5.7, 4.5.4). Nobody is left who may sign it. manifests/reactions.json reads it as a verdict withdrawn on the target, with no notice. Adjacent to C390, which covers the vote-against case.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1 **(3) Self-revocation** is recognised when the revoker's own key digests to the subject, whether or not `revoked_key_id` is present.
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json key:revocation attest roles: ["self"] (formal/derivation/transition_text.tsv, cited to CC 2.4.1.1)
note: The text has a `revoking_key_id` distinct from the revoked key, judges "the revoker's authority ... without the subject's record" (CC 3.1.3) and treats self-revocation as one case. The transition admits the attest for role `self` only, so a kernel that executes the table refuses a revocation signed by any other key. This reader takes `self` to mean signer equals subject, as on session and census:share; if the token means the revoker's own key, there is no finding.

side_a: CC 3.2 "the halt latch **as it reaches this node** ([CC 4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md): a live accord edge at the halt's `asserted_at`)"
side_b: CC 4.2.1 "A halt is active at a node from the instant the node's store admits the row and latches ([CC 4.2.1.1](#4.2.1.1)). The signer-chosen `asserted_at` plays no part"
note: T8's inputs list restates the halt's reach at the signer's asserted_at; the home judges the edge at the node's own latch and says asserted_at plays no part. A node that cut its edge after the halt was signed and before it arrived is bound under T8's wording and free under CC 4.2.1; a sealed halt signed long ago flips the other way. This is the wording C033 records as removed from CC 4.2.1; it survives in CC 3.2. CC 4.2.1, 4.2.1.1 and 4.4.3.8 support the latch.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "An affiliation withdraws no statement about itself, whatever the statement. Its path is reconsideration and the reader's composition."
note: 155 families take the default lifecycle and a withdraw transition for roles author, subject with no guard typed. Nothing in transitions.json, guard_text.tsv or the lifecycle cells closes the subject arm to a subject that is an affiliation, so a kernel run from the data admits an affiliation's withdrawal of a review, rating or complaint naming it. CC 2.4.1.1 and CC 4.4.3.2.8 agree it never retracts.

side_a: CC 2.4.1: "on any edge carrying `sub_delegation`, `license`, `grant`, `moderate`, `takedown`, `review` or `slash`, or sitting in an affiliation's `hierarchy`"
side_b: data formal/derivation/reaction_text.tsv: "@affiliations expiry required delegation_valid_until default delegation_term_max_secs max charter.role_term from delegation_valid_from"
note: Text against data. The one typed expiry on a delegation (reactions.json, trust:{job}:{version}: required delegation_valid_until, bounded by the term ceiling) is scoped to affiliations. CC 2.4.1 and the CC 2.6.1.7 row require the term, at most 365 days, on every edge that carries an issuance or moderation scope in a group of any kind, and refuse a perpetual or over-ceiling one delegation_term_required. The family's subject_rule cell (code-v61) does say a term is required, so the data disagrees with itself; but run from the reactions, a moderate, takedown, license or grant edge in a family or community has no ceiling and no lapse, and the reaction that locks a room when its moderate edge expires never fires there.
